title: Study
description: One Deep Study unit for a passage of the Quran. Sections appear in the app in the order declared here. Word bounds live in x-wordBounds and are enforced by validate.mjs.

theme.description: Human-readable theme shown in the pill above the title, e.g. "Patience in Trials".

title.description: Short evocative title for this passage, 2-8 words, title case, no trailing punctuation.

tier.description: discover = curated Discover feed unit; core = named/landmark passage; standard = everything else.

meaning.description: What the passage means, in plain accessible English. 45-105 words.

historicalContext.description: Where and when it was revealed and what was happening. Mention asbab al-nuzul only when it is well attested. 40-90 words.

arabic.description: The term in Arabic script exactly as it appears in the passage. Arabic script only - never a transliteration.

gloss.description: English gloss, 1-6 words, no Arabic script.

note.description: What the word carries that the English translation cannot. 15-45 words, no Arabic script.

lifeInProphetsTime.description: Everyday life in seventh-century Arabia that makes the passage land. 40-90 words.
lifeInProphetsTime.$comment: Rendered under the heading 'Life in the Prophet's Time'.

didYouKnow.description: One surprising, verifiable fact about the passage, surah, or its language. 30-80 words.

theologicalSignificance.description: What the passage establishes about God, revelation, or the human being. 40-95 words.

ref.description: Another passage of the Quran, e.g. "39:53".

why.description: One clause saying how it connects. 8-30 words.

applyIt.description: One concrete thing the reader can do today, in the second person. 30-80 words.

explainEasier.description: The passage as you would tell it to a twelve-year-old: what it is saying, in the plainest words that stay true. 25-50 words, grade 6 or below, no Arabic script. Optional - written by the simplify pass (`author.mjs rewrite`) and shown in the reader's verse menu under 'Explain Easier'.

simplified.description: The promptVersion of the simplify pass this unit has been through, e.g. "p1". Present only on rewritten units; it is what makes validate.mjs enforce x-readability as errors rather than warnings.

author.description: Who wrote the rewrite, e.g. "opus-session". Stamped alongside `simplified`.

x-readability.$comment: Flesch-Kincaid grade ceilings, measured by lib/readability.mjs. validate.mjs reports a miss as an error on units whose meta.simplified is set and as a warning on the rest, so the corpus that predates the simplify pass still validates.
